messages.subject: Boosting
messages.body_plain:
Hi All…

Firstly, I am really learning a lot from this user group…. Thanks to all those who post.

My problem lies with the use of Boosting. I have tried many data sets, and while Rattle allows me to apply decision trees and random foresting to these data sets, it does not allow me to undertake boosting. I have checked the data, and I can see no reason why this should be the case. Perhaps im missing something.

Can anyone enlighten me as to why this might be happening?

Look forward to hearing from you.

Cheers

John

messages.subject: Re: Boosting
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jono,

I'll update the tooltip and help page for this. The Boost option uses "ada" and as per the ada man page

> ?ada

[...]
‘ada’ is used to fit a variety stochastic boosting models for a binary response

So the Boost option is only available for binary classification (i.e., a categoric target with two levels). I'm guessing your data does not have a binary target.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: GLM Pmml Bug due to substring match
messages.subject_clean: GLM Pmml Bug due to substring match
messages.body_plain:
There is a bug in the pmml glm package Below is the detail of the bug

PMML glm package does substring matching for parameters to predictor matching. Hence if we have column names that have similar names PPCell gets all the  predictors - parameter matches. Below is an example of this.

data = read.csv("~/test.csv", check.names = FALSE)
df = cbind(data)
fit = glm(out~.,data=df)
library(pmml)
pmml.glm(fit)

test.csv
Test This,Test This 2,out
10,12,0
12,23,1
12,10,0

If you see the "Test This" is a substring of "Test This 2"

  <ParameterList>
   <Parameter name="p0" label="(Intercept)"/>
   <Parameter name="p1" label="`Test This`"/>
   <Parameter name="p2" label="`Test This 2`"/>
  </ParameterList>
  <FactorList/>
  <CovariateList>
   <Predictor name="Test This"/>
   <Predictor name="Test This 2"/>
  </CovariateList>
  <PPMatrix>
   <PPCell value="1" predictorName="Test This" parameterName="p1"/>
   <PPCell value="1" predictorName="Test This" parameterName="p2"/>
   <PPCell value="1" predictorName="Test This 2" parameterName="p2"/>
  </PPMatrix>
  <ParamMatrix>
   <PCell parameterName="p0" df="1" beta="-1.6923076923077"/>
   <PCell parameterName="p1" df="1" beta="0.0769230769230773"/>
   <PCell parameterName="p2" df="1" beta="0.0769230769230769"/>
  </ParamMatrix>
 </GeneralRegressionModel>
</PMML>

For the PPCell value for p2 which corresponds to only "Test This 2" has both the predictors. Which will screw up the scoring as co-effieicents of the second variable get multiplied to the product of "Test This" and "Test This 2" rather than just "Test This 2"

Below is the glm output

Call:  glm(formula = out ~ ., data = df)

Coefficients:
  (Intercept)    `Test This`  `Test This 2`
     -1.69231        0.07692        0.07692

Degrees of Freedom: 2 Total (i.e. Null);  0 Residual
Null Deviance:        0.6667
Residual Deviance: 1.245e-30     AIC: -193.4

Looks like there are bunch of greps that might be causing these problems

 if(length(grep(field$name[f],strsplit(names(coefficients(model))[j],":")[[1]][k])) == 1){

Regards
Girish S Kathalagiri

messages.subject: Re: Error in as.GType(type) : Cannot convert RGtkBuilder to GType
messages.subject_clean: Error in as.GType(type) : Cannot convert RGtkBuilder to GType
messages.body_plain:
Could this be the issue noted on: http://rattle.togaware.com/rattle-install-troubleshooting.html

Error in as.GType(type) : Cannot convert RGtkBuilder to GType

This will often be displayed if you have not restarted R after installing the GTK+ libraries. It will also be displayed if the GTK+ libraries (which are installed separately to R itself) have not been installed. On MS/Windows this can also occur if there are conflicts in your PATH, such as when there are multiple GTK+ libraries found in your PATH and you are running R32 but it finds GTK64 first.

Graham Williams
http://togaware.com

messages.body_plain:
I am probably the world's worst R programmer.
But I can give you a suggestion for your first question.

There are many ways to filter the data, but one that I think has the easiest syntax for newbies like me is the subset function.

If you want to subset records based on a logical filter, you use the function like this:

     newDataFrame<-as.data.frame(subset(originalDataFrame,variableYouAreFilteringOn==1))

You could then select newDataFrame in rattle as your data source.

Ignore the following aside if you don't care:
-------------------------------------------------------

Just so you don't get confused if you look at the documentation for subset, it can also be used to filter which variables you want to keep in the dataset.

If you want to drop a few variables, the syntax is like this (notice the minus sign):

      newDataFrame<-as.data.frame(subset(originalDataFrame,select=-c(firstVariableToDrop,secondVariableToDrop)))

If you want to only keep certain specified variables, the syntax is like this:

      newDataFrame<-as.data.frame(subset(originalDataFrame,select=-c(firstVariableToDrop,secondVariableToDrop)))
-------------------------------------------------------

You can also use the bracket [] function to subset variables, which I do use occasionally, but I usually still use subset b/c the syntax is easier.  Someone better at R can probably give an overview of using the bracket function.

I could stumble through manually creating a variable for all the combinations of x and y, but I don't think I'm the best to give you advice on that.  Perhaps there is an elegant package that would make the task more straightforward.

Scott
